title: Diagnostics on Data Ministries Already Hold

slides.title: Diagnostics on Data Ministries Already Hold
slides.subtitle: Three climate-fiscal analytics tools: papers 5.1–5.3
slides.message: Analysis changes policy only when the ministry that holds the budget can reproduce it. Each tool takes data the ministry already holds, puts it on a common scale and returns a sequenced answer.

slides.title: The reproducibility standard
slides.text: A diagnostic a ministry cannot check is a recommendation it must take on trust.
points: Every intermediate step visible; every value carries its source and year.
Defaults defended line by line, with ranges where evidence is thin.
AI drafts under a written specification; every line is checked against the source.

slides.title: Excise: two countries, two different gaps
slides.caption: Excise-Fiscal Diagnostic, 2026 runs on Sierra Leone and Liberia; illustrative results, not official estimates (5.1).
points: Any schedule mapped onto 30 standard lines and scaled three ways.
Sierra Leone: excise 1.3% of GDP, about 90% from fuel at $0.23 per liter.
Liberia: excise 0.4% of GDP; fuel levies of $0.095 per liter, below the carbon cost alone.
Both: health excises legislated but weakly collected.

slides.title: Scenario tool: financing beats size
slides.caption: GIMF-lite, stylized program of 1% of GDP a year for ten years (5.2).
points: One workbook for 186 countries: needs, pricing, lite macro models, debt test.
Kenya: budget need 0.5% of GDP in 2030, mostly land use and non-CO₂.
Power-sector pricing covers about 5%; debt +7 points by 2050.

slides.title: Dashboard: a one-page profile from public data
slides.caption: 2024 values from IMF WoRLD and WEO, as compiled by the pipeline (5.3).
points: 80 indicators, 12 blocks, 217 economies, about twenty public datasets.
Never imputes; stops if configuration and output disagree.
Indonesia: a revenue problem. South Africa: a debt-service problem.
No overall index: the triage is the point.
